{"summary": "Controls part is done: the mouse fix, crouch, sprint and snappier movement are in. The mouse fix is verified in headless Chrome, not in Opera. The carry, cart, play and eat bots pass or fail for reasons I could not tie to movement (see issues).

**1. Mouse bug**
- **Cause:** Godot's own web code asks for pointer lock from its main loop, not inside the click. The old game code turned the camera whenever Godot reported `mouse_mode == CAPTURED`, even if the browser never held the lock. A free cursor's `movementX` then kept turning the view until the cursor hit the screen edge (the "wall"). This is the most likely cause; I could not reproduce it in Opera itself.
- **Fix:** new `components/mouse_lock.gd` installs a JS listener through JavaScriptBridge on pointerdown/mousedown.
  - It calls `canvas.requestPointerLock({unadjustedMovement:true})` synchronously inside the click.
  - It falls back to a plain request on `NotSupportedError`.
  - It retries once, timed to the Esc cooldown, after a `SecurityError`.
- **Turning only under a real lock:** the camera turns only while the browser really holds the lock.
- **Lost lock:** if Godot is CAPTURED but there is no real lock for 1.5 s, or the browser refused, the game switches to VISIBLE at once. The click-to-play card shows and the next click relocks.
- **Wiring:** `entities/actor.gd` (turning and clicks) and `entities/spectator_camera.gd` use `MouseLock.held()`.
- **Spike filter:** after a lock, a jump over 60 px in the first 3 events is dropped. The Firefox drift filter stays, and only runs when the user agent is Firefox, so it can't eat a real turn in Chromium or Opera.
- **F3 overlay:** `world/hud/mouse_diag.gd` shows the browser, Godot mode, real lock flag, last movementX/Y, events per second and lock errors.
- **Research:** `mouse.md` has the sources and the FPS speed numbers. The Source-engine acceleration figures there are from memory, not verified.

- The capsule goes from 1.8 m to 1.2 m with feet fixed. The eye and shoulder drop `Actor.CROUCH_DROP` (the camera eases). Walk speed is ×0.45.

Swing (world/chop/axe_swing.gd, AxeSwing, pure and deterministic):
- The head travels on a circle about the shoulder; crouching lowers the shoulder by Actor.CROUCH_DROP (binary meta, same on server, pilot and bots). A one-hand left swing uses the left shoulder and mirrors the direction.
- The swing plane is spanned by shoulder→aim point and the camera right axis, turned by InputSystem.swing_of (wheel, 15° steps).
- Radius = distance to what the look meets + DRIVE 4 cm, clamped to 0.72–1 × Impact.reach_of. Targets further away are reached by bending/leaning: the pivot moves up to BEND_MAX 0.95 m toward them.
- The edge lies along the radius, the head travels along the tangent. The cheeks open at the edge half-angle up to the eye thickness, and the haft trails behind.
- contact(): coarse key-point sweep, then fine 1 cm steps over edge, cheek and haft probes, then bisection. The first wood any probe touches stops the head. If a cheek or the haft touches first with no edge in the wood, the marker turns red ("jam").

Cut:
- The head goes on along the arc while σ·KAPPA/ETA·V(head∩wood) stays within the blow energy (Impact.wood's law on the real cut trunk). Cheeks in an open V cost nothing; cheeks against a narrow kerf cost a lot. Nothing goes past the eye, so no hole deeper than the head's own height.
- Removed wood = the head wedge at its stop + a chip prism. The chip splits along the grain toward the nearest free face (side/up rule). Its length is kl·depth·|n·grain|·PACE (PACE 2.0, the only fudge), capped at 2 × head length. A free face beside the chip within 1.5 × depth takes the strip between too.

Wood model (world/chop/wood_cuts.gd, WoodCuts):
- Convex pieces given as planes. Exact accounting by 5 mm slices along the grain, each touched slice a cell bitmap (3–7 mm cells; untouched slices are the analytic disk).
- Removed volume = cleared cells × cell volume, so chips equal removed wood to the cell.
- solid(p) is an O(1) bit test. A coarse 24×24 fibre mask per slice feeds the strength check: fibres intact over ±FIBRE_BAND carry the top; bending stress / MOR as before decides the fall.

- From the free face that Spall.free_face finds, it fits the exterior face's plane from the rock's own triangles. It then sets the edge, the exterior platform angle, and the platform thickness PT (how deep the struck point lies behind the face).
- The crack starts at the ring round the contact. It dips toward the core at the cone half-angle by kind (granite 52°, sandstone 58°, limestone 62°), which makes the bulb. Then it runs down the face at depth PT.
- Past the platform it follows the stone's real outer surface, sampled on a 13×15 grid, so convex faces give shorter flakes on their own.
- Potential run length is PT × (1.2 + 2.3·g(platform angle)).
- Roughness is deterministic noise per kind: granite coarse with facets, sandstone grainy, limestone fine with ripples. The grid is jittered so facets don't repeat.
- Bedded kinds: when beds cross the run, the crack turns onto a bed, and across the width part of it steps to the next bed. When beds lie along the face, the crack terraces onto them. Bed cracks cost less (Fabric.plane_factor per facet), and a bed lets the flake spread sideways by 1/√r.
- Energy is the same Spall crack budget as before. If the full run costs too much, the run is shortened: feather becomes hinge, then step, then crush only.
- The cutter is a closed non-convex heightfield mesh. Chunk = rock ∩ cutter (CSG on CpuMesh); scar = rock minus it.

  "summary": "Tree part, task 52. Chopping is now a physical axe flight instead of \"the cut appears at the crosshair\".\n\nSwing (world/chop/axe_swing.gd, AxeSwing, pure and deterministic):\n- The head travels on a circle about the shoulder; crouching lowers the shoulder by Actor.CROUCH_DROP (binary meta, same on server, pilot and bots). A one-hand left swing uses the left shoulder and mirrors the direction.\n- The swing plane is spanned by shoulder→aim point and the camera right axis, turned by InputSystem.swing_of (wheel, 15° steps).\n- Radius = distance to what the look meets + DRIVE 4 cm, clamped to 0.72–1 × Impact.reach_of. Targets further away are reached by bending/leaning: the pivot moves up to BEND_MAX 0.95 m toward them.\n- The edge lies along the radius, the head travels along the tangent. The cheeks open at the edge half-angle up to the eye thickness, and the haft trails behind.\n- contact(): coarse key-point sweep, then fine 1 cm steps over edge, cheek and haft probes, then bisection. The first wood any probe touches stops the head. If a cheek or the haft touches first with no edge in the wood, the marker turns red (\"jam\").\n\nCut:\n- The head goes on along the arc while σ·KAPPA/ETA·V(head∩wood) stays within the blow energy (Impact.wood's law on the real cut trunk). Cheeks in an open V cost nothing; cheeks against a narrow kerf cost a lot. Nothing goes past the eye, so no hole deeper than the head's own height.\n- Removed wood = the head wedge at its stop + a chip prism. The chip splits along the grain toward the nearest free face (side/up rule). Its length is kl·depth·|n·grain|·PACE (PACE 2.0, the only fudge), capped at 2 × head length. A free face beside the chip within 1.5 × depth takes the strip between too.\n\nWood model (world/chop/wood_cuts.gd, WoodCuts):\n- Convex pieces given as planes. Exact accounting by 5 mm slices along the grain, each touched slice a cell bitmap (3–7 mm cells; untouched slices are the analytic disk).\n- Removed volume = cleared cells × cell volume, so chips equal removed wood to the cell.\n- solid(p) is an O(1) bit test. A coarse 24×24 fibre mask per slice feeds the strength check: fibres intact over ±FIBRE_BAND carry the top; bending stress / MOR as before decides the fall.\n\nChopTree rewrite:\n- apply_blow(flat planes, counts, point, into); the server sends pieces via rpc _tree_blow and every peer applies the same planes.\n- The CSG is split into 0.15 m bands, 24 sectors, 8 pieces per group, so a blow redoes only the bands it reaches. Log bucking goes through BuildSystem.buck(peer, {tree, aim, energy, tool}).\n\nBuildSystem (my parts only):\n- buck() and log_solid() use the same arc/cut.   "summary": "I finished all five ground items, but multiplayer is untested and two bots fail (cart_glade, build_glade); both failures look like other parts' changes. Once a log lies still it sends one event with the log's pose and its sink depth; every peer then builds the same plan. After that the server sends the plan's steps one per 2 ticks: first the log is pressed into the soil, then the litter goes down one 4 m patch at a time.\n- Litter volume = (foliage + fine-branch share for the species) × stem dry mass, compacted to forest-floor soil at 130 kg/m³. It is added to DigLayer in exact whole units (new `deposit()`). The new counter `litter_in` is printed; `soil_sum() - litter_in` stays constant.\n- **Crown choice:** I removed the crown with the litter rather than thinning it. The green crown browns and folds onto the stem over 2.6 s while flakes fall, then only bare branch sticks lie on the ground. It reads as a clear cause and effect: the crown turns into the carpet under it.\n- Because the crown now goes, I switched off `FallCrown.press` (`PRESS = false`). That removes a mesh read-back, which is a GPU stall on the web.\n- **Look:** both ground shaders show needles orange-brown and leaves yellow-brown. They darken to humus and then fade back to turf on a litter clock (1 year = 60 s of game time): a pine reaches humus in about 4 min, a birch in about 1.5 min. Grass tufts still poke through the litter.\n\n**Log sinks in.** The fall's energy (0.3 × m·g·h of the top's centre of mass) crushes soft topsoil (100 kPa). That gives a trough a few cm deep, capped at 20 % of the diameter; for example a 26 cm pine sinks 3.7 cm. The log is first let down to where its bark meets the soil, then sunk, and DigLayer's new `press_log()` pushes the trough's soil into berms on both sides, conserved. Previously its radius + 0.3 m was blocked; this uses a new obstacle filter in DigLayer plus `reblock()`.\n- The roots hold the stump as long as enough soil stays round it. Their hold starts at 15 kN for a 25 cm stump (growing with d²) and drops with the square of the ring soil left. After each dig the server compares that hold with what the digger can pry with (fit: 1.08 kN).\n- When it gives, the stump becomes a loose Timber (the build part's loose wood) with a roots mesh. **Fixes to make the parts work together**
- **First-cut stall in the browser removed.**
  - Cause: PineMesh.bend read each tree's mesh back from the GPU, so the first blow on any tree froze the browser for 2.2–3.2 s.
  - Fix: pine_mesh.gd now keeps a CPU copy of each mesh it builds (`_with_cpu`, `arrays_of`, which hands out fresh copies). valley_forest.gd and glade_forest.gd use that copy too, so trees streaming in on the valley no longer read meshes back either.
  - Result: the first blow went from 3161 ms to 55–157 ms.
- **Bots fed the felling planner a stale number.** range_bot, build_bot and showcase_bot passed the previous hit's chip volume to `ChopTechnique.after_blow`. After a swing through air, the planner kept the useless stance, and about 110 of 120 strikes on an oak missed. They now pass the real volume removed by that blow.
- **build_bot:** felling uses ChopTechnique with a 120-strike budget. Its bucking checks now use ChopTechnique stances, one by real input and one by the server's own cut through `buck()`.
- **break_bot:** the post cut now picks the swing direction and distance whose landing is nearest the wanted height, so the upper part of the post falls (`fence_upper_fell`).
- **cart_bot:** the trunk test picks a trunk ahead of the cart with a clear path and steers the cart, not the body, at it. The trunk gap went from 2.08 m to 0.15 m.
- **HUD:**
  - Long hints wrap in the middle and no longer run under the section inset (`_say` sizes the box itself).
  - The start card hides the hands bar, so "Кликни, чтобы начать" is visible at 960x540.

The last full run (R4, done under hub load of about 100) had three failures that depend on wall-clock time; each passed when rerun on its own (details in issues). The final web build is in build/web-integ. It was checked in headless Chrome on the valley through the full set of 17 screenshots plus 3 valley tour views, and I looked at every screenshot. Nothing was committed or published.

**Fixes to make the parts work together**
- **First-cut stall in the browser removed.**
  - Cause: PineMesh.bend read each tree's mesh back from the GPU, so the first blow on any tree froze the browser for 2.2–3.2 s.
  - Fix: pine_mesh.gd now keeps a CPU copy of each mesh it builds (`_with_cpu`, `arrays_of`, which hands out fresh copies). valley_forest.gd and glade_forest.gd use that copy too, so trees streaming in on the valley no longer read meshes back either.
  - Result: the first blow went from 3161 ms to 55–157 ms.
- **Bots fed the felling planner a stale number.** range_bot, build_bot and showcase_bot passed the previous hit's chip volume to `ChopTechnique.after_blow`. After a swing through air, the planner kept the useless stance, and about 110 of 120 strikes on an oak missed. They now pass the real volume removed by that blow.
- **build_bot:** felling uses ChopTechnique with a 120-strike budget. Its bucking checks now use ChopTechnique stances, one by real input and one by the server's own cut th
